# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** Mid-forties  <sub>[v1 c29 P11](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0011)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c26 P5](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v1 c29 P10](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0010)</sub>
- **Origin:** East Welby, St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v1 c27 P16](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0016)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v1 c26 P5](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0005)</sub>; Mrs.  <sub>[v1 c29 P10](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0010)</sub>

## Appearance

Rosalind Penrose is a petite, remarkably attractive woman who possesses a youthful, rosy-cheeked complexion with dimples and large, expressive brown eyes. She has a fine, smooth forehead and thick, wavy, snow-white hair that she styles in flattering puffs and coils. Her voice is sweet and clear, and she has a penchant for youthful, frilly attire such as light muslin dresses.

_Sources: [v1 c29 P18](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0018), [v1 c33 P8](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0008), [v1 c33 P18](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0018)_

## Personality

Rosalind is romantic, imaginative, and youthful in spirit, often engaging in playful pretense to escape loneliness. She possesses a cheerful and sweet disposition, yet can be moody, proud, and stubborn when her emotions are hurt. She loves company and delights in entertaining guests with elaborate teas and treats. Despite her imaginative tendencies, she is also capable of great warmth, understanding, and deep affection.

_Sources: [v1 c27 P19](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0019), [v1 c29 P19](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0019), [v1 c29 P32](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0032)_

## Traits

- Imaginative
- Proud  <sub>[v1 c27 P19](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0019)</sub>
- Hospitable
- Youthful at heart  <sub>[v1 c29 P18](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0018)</sub>
- Moody  <sub>[v1 c27 P19](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0019)</sub>

## Abilities

- Baking and hospitality
- Storytelling and pretense

## Goals

- To find companionship and romance to dispel loneliness
- To reunite with her true love, Stephen Stanhope  <sub>[v1 c27 P19](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0019), [v1 c28 P35](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0035)</sub>

## History

Rosalind Penrose lived for decades in seclusion at Echo Cottage in Middle Welby following a broken engagement with Stephen Stanhope in her youth. To cope with her isolation, she frequently engaged in imaginative games and hosted pretend tea parties for non-existent guests. Eventually, Nell Harcourt accidentally stumbled upon Echo Cottage and struck up a close friendship with her. After learning of Rosalind's past, Nell helped arrange a reunion between Rosalind and Stephen Stanhope when he returned to St. Brendan's Island to visit his son Cedric. The two reconciled, fell in love anew, and were married twenty-five years after their initial breakup in an outdoor ceremony at Echo Cottage. Following the wedding, she and Stephen departed for a journey to the Pacific Coast, planning to reside in Boston while keeping Echo Cottage for summer visits.

_Sources: [v1 c26 P5](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0005), [v1 c27 P19](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0019), [v1 c28 P35](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0035), [v1 c29 P10](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0010), [v1 c29 P11](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0011)_

## Background by volume

- Her father named her Rosalind because of his love for lavender
- Was engaged in her youth to Stephen Stanhope before a foolish quarrel separated them  <sub>[v1 c27 P16](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0016), [v1 c27 P19](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0019)</sub>
- Remained unmarried and lived alone at Echo Cottage for decades after Stephen left for the United States  <sub>[v1 c26 P5](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0005), [v1 c27 P16](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0016), [v1 c27 P19](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0019)</sub>
- Employed a succession of young girls named Belinda to help her with housechores

## Quotes

> Fancies and imaginings suffice perfectly well during daylight hours and under bright skies, yet they fall short of comforting us once nightfall and tempest arrive.  <sub>[v1 c27 P11](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0011)</sub>

> I will refrain from making a single excuse for myself. I was a foolish, flirtatious girl, and I enjoyed teasing Stephen.  <sub>[v1 c27 P19](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0019)</sub>

> A broken heart in real life is not nearly as romantic or as tragic as it is in books. It is very much like a decayed tooth.  <sub>[v1 c27 P19](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0019)</sub>
